definition: The International Journal of Approximate Reasoning is a monthly peer-reviewed scientific journal in artificial intelligence.
details: It was established in 1987 by Jim Bezdek and is published by Elsevier, with Thierry Denoeux as its editor-in-chief.
story: Picture solving a puzzle by talking yourself through it out loud — wrong turns, second guesses, and all — until the answer clicks. It writes its thinking down, reads it back, and fixes the parts that do not hold up. Slowing down to think often beats answering fast. It is thinking made visible — the model shows its work, then reads its own work and improves it. And that habit of thinking twice — or a hundred times — is International Journal of Approximate Reasoning.
